- U1: WebSocket source module
- U2: AWS source module (S3, SES)
- U3: Cassandra sink
- U4: AWS sink (S3)
- U5: HAWQ sink (via PXF, Avro/Parquet)
- U6: SOLR sink
- U7: Error channel configuration (global error handling)
- U8: Data partition strategy state preservation (testing effort only)

This looks like Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring Cloud Stream modules (the old "spring-xd" style modules - source, processor, sink). The specification mentions "source module", "sink", "stream.module" naming like "topic.errors.stream.module" - this is Spring XD / Spring Cloud Stream app starters style.

Common infrastructure:
- Project setup, module scaffolding, build configuration (Maven/Gradle), Spring Boot starters for each module
- Common module archetype/parent config

U1: WebSocket source module
- Design + implement WebSocket inbound channel adapter based on Spring Integration WebSocket support
- Configuration properties, server setup
- Unit tests, integration tests
- Documentation

U2: AWS source module (S3, SES)
- S3 inbound channel adapter (streaming/sync), SES inbound (via SNS/SQS typically)
- Credentials/config properties
- Tests (LocalStack), docs

U3: Cassandra sink
- Outbound channel adapter/message handler writing to Cassandra
- Schema mapping, consistency config, batching
- Tests (embedded/testcontainers), docs

U4: AWS sink (S3)
- S3 message handler, key naming strategy, multipart upload
- Tests, docs

U5: HAWQ sink via PXF with Avro/Parquet
- More complex: write to HDFS in Avro/Parquet, PXF external table integration
- Tests (hard to test - need HAWQ/Hadoop test env), docs

U6: SOLR sink
- SolrJ-based message handler, collection config, field mapping
- Tests (embedded solr), docs

U7: Error channel
- Global error channel infrastructure, error message enhancement (preserve Caused by), exception hierarchy (GlobalException, DefaultException, ModuleSpecificException), configurable catch patterns
- Integration with all modules
- Tests, docs

U8: Partition strategy state testing
- Test effort only: dynamic scaling tests with add/delete modules

Cross-cutting:
- Integration/end-to-end tests
- CI/CD pipeline setup
- Documentation aggregate
- Release packaging

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement each user story as an independent Spring Boot / Spring Integration module following the source/sink module model (analogous to Spring Cloud Stream app starters), packaged as a standalone executable jar with externalized configuration properties and configuration-metadata.
Target Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot 3, per the specification's baseline requirements.
U1 WebSocket source is built on the existing Spring Integration WebSocket support (server-side inbound WebSocket channel adapter), not a from-scratch WebSocket server.

U2 AWS source and U4 AWS sink are built on the Spring Integration AWS extension: S3 inbound adapter (polling/streaming) plus SES ingestion via SNS/SQS notification pipeline; S3 sink via the S3 message handler with configurable key-naming and multipart upload.
U3 Cassandra sink uses the DataStax Java driver / Spring Data Cassandra with configurable keyspace, table mapping, consistency level and batching.
U5 HAWQ sink writes files to HDFS in Avro/Parquet format and registers/provisions PXF external tables so HAWQ can read them; PXF DDL generation is part of the module.
U6 SOLR sink uses SolrJ with configurable collection, field mapping and commit strategy.

U7 is implemented as shared error-handling infrastructure usable by every module: a configurable global error channel (default binding named like 'topic.errors.stream.module'), a configurable catch pattern (default '**Exception'), an exception hierarchy (GlobalException -> DefaultException / ModuleSpecificException), and an error-message enricher that traverses the exception chain to preserve the root 'Caused by:' and stages the error as the channel payload while ingestion continues.
A single Maven multi-module build with a shared parent POM, common module archetype, and CI pipeline (build, unit tests, integration tests) is set up once and reused by all modules.
Integration tests use Testcontainers/LocalStack (AWS), embedded/Testcontainers Cassandra, and embedded Solr; U5 uses a dedicated Hadoop/HAWQ test environment.

U8 requires no new production code (feature already in GA); the effort covers designing and executing regression/scaling tests that add and remove modules while verifying partition-strategy state is preserved.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; all figures are effort (work-hours), not elapsed calendar time.

The referenced Spring Integration WebSocket support and Spring Integration AWS extension are reused as libraries; the work is building and packaging the source/sink modules around them, not reimplementing the extensions.
The underlying stream runtime/deployment platform already exists (GA) and provides module deployment, binding and partitioning infrastructure; only U8's testing effort is in scope for that area.
Sandbox accounts/environments are available for testing: AWS (or LocalStack), a Cassandra cluster, a Solr server, and a Hadoop/HAWQ cluster with PXF for U5 integration tests.
No user interface work is required; modules are configured purely through properties/YAML.
Documentation scope is limited to per-module READMEs, configuration-property metadata and a short aggregated reference section.
The developer is experienced with Spring Integration; the only significant learning curve is HAWQ/PXF specifics for U5, which is reflected in its higher estimate.
Per-module estimates include unit tests; integration/E2E testing that spans multiple modules is estimated separately.
Requirements are stable; no rework due to changing requirements is included.

activities.activity_description: Analyze U1-U8, define module contracts (source/sink interfaces, payload formats, property namespaces), error-handling architecture, and produce the overall design for the increment.

activities.activity_name: Project scaffolding, build and CI setup
activities.activity_description: Create Maven multi-module project, shared parent POM, module archetype, dependency management, configuration-metadata generation, and CI pipeline (compile, unit test, integration test stages).
Implement the WebSocket source module using Spring Integration WebSocket support: server endpoint, inbound channel adapter wiring, message mapping of browser events, and configuration properties.
Unit tests and integration tests with a WebSocket client simulating browser sessions, covering connect/disconnect, message ingestion and error paths.

activities.activity_name: U2 AWS source module (S3, SES) - implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement the AWS source using the Spring Integration AWS extension: S3 inbound adapter (polling/streaming of new objects) and SES ingestion via SNS/SQS notification pipeline, with credential/region configuration properties.
Unit tests and LocalStack/Testcontainers-based integration tests for S3 ingestion and the SES notification flow.
Implement the Cassandra sink message handler: connection/session management, configurable keyspace/table and field mapping, consistency level, batching and high-throughput write tuning.
Unit tests plus integration tests against an embedded/Testcontainers Cassandra instance, including throughput-oriented write scenarios.
Implement the S3 sink message handler: bucket/key naming strategy (SpEL-driven), content-type handling, multipart upload for large payloads, and retry/ACL configuration.
Unit tests and LocalStack-based integration tests verifying object creation, key naming, metadata and failure handling.
Implement the HAWQ sink: write data files to HDFS in Avro/Parquet format, generate/execute PXF external table DDL, manage file rollover and partitioning, and expose configuration properties.
Unit tests plus integration tests against a Hadoop/HAWQ test environment validating Avro/Parquet output and PXF external table readability.
Implement the SOLR sink using SolrJ: configurable collection/core, field mapping, document conversion, commit/soft-commit strategy and batching for full-text indexing.
Unit tests and integration tests against an embedded/standalone Solr server, verifying indexing, searchability and commit behavior.

Implement global error channel support: configurable error channel binding (e.g., 'topic.errors.stream.module'), configurable catch pattern (e.g., 'catch=**Exception'), exception hierarchy (GlobalException -> DefaultException -> ModuleSpecificException), and error-message enrichment that traverses the exception chain to preserve the root 'Caused by:' as the staged payload while ingestion continues.
Unit and integration tests covering failures at source, processor and sink modules (custom and built-in), cause-chain traversal, payload staging and routing to the error channel.

activities.activity_name: U8 Partition strategy state preservation - testing
activities.activity_description: Design and execute regression tests that dynamically add and delete modules/partitions and verify the partition strategy state is preserved and modules adapt correctly (testing effort only; feature already in GA).
End-to-end stream tests combining sources and sinks (e.g., WebSocket->Cassandra, AWS S3->SOLR, HTTP source with error channel routing per U7 scenario) across the deployed modules.
Per-module READMEs, configuration property reference, error-channel configuration guide (U7) and aggregated reference documentation for the increment.
Versioning, building releasable artifacts (jars), publishing module metadata, and smoke-verifying deployment of each module in the runtime.
